settings.content: Palette, spacing, radius and motion are NOT theme settings. They live in the design system and resolve through assets/theme.css — exposing them here would let one edit break the whole system. Only copy and the type pairing are editable.

settings.label: Brand description
settings.info: Used for the meta description and Open Graph. Leave blank and no tag is emitted rather than an empty one.
settings.default: Handwoven linen and cotton, sewn in small runs in Bandung.

settings.content: The design system's pairing: Playfair Display carries the editorial voice, Poppins is the interface. Changing either is a design-system decision, not a shop decision.
The espresso strip above the header. Nothing in it is interactive — a bar that carries a link competes with the nav directly underneath it. Leave blank and the whole band is not rendered.

settings.label: Message
settings.default: Free shipping on orders over Rp 750.000

settings.content: The two values the B2B route and the Shopee hand-off depend on. Both are blank today, and both fail visibly rather than silently: with no WhatsApp number the quote form's button is unavailable and says why, and with no Shopee URL the 'Buy on Shopee' link is simply absent instead of landing on a search page.

settings.label: WhatsApp number
settings.info: In international format. The + and any spaces or dashes are stripped before the link is built, so either form works. This is where every quote enquiry goes — there is no inbox behind the form. Supplied by the studio 2026-09-13 and set as the schema default rather than written into config/settings_data.json, which this theme deliberately does not have: a default is a starting value the studio can still change in the theme editor, whereas a committed settings file would silently overwrite their edit on the next push.

settings.label: Shopee shop URL
settings.info: The fallback for products with no custom.shopee_url metafield of their own. A per-product URL always wins, because it lands the shopper on the piece rather than on the shop.

settings.content: The size chart shown on every product page. It is store-wide on purpose: Wear Label has one size system, and a per-product chart would be the same table typed eleven times and eleven places to correct when one number is wrong. A product that genuinely needs its own chart can still carry a custom.size_chart metafield, and that wins over this.

settings.label: Column headings
settings.default: Size, Waist, Hip, Rise, Inseam, Leg opening
settings.info: Comma separated. The FIRST one names the size column. These are trouser measurements because almost everything in the catalogue is trousers — change them if that changes.

settings.label: Rows
settings.info: One size per line, values separated by | and in the same order as the headings above. For example: XS | 64 | 90 | 28 | 72 | 26. Type CENTIMETRES only — the inch column is calculated. Leave this blank and the chart renders a labelled placeholder at its final size rather than a wrong table.

settings.label: Note under the chart
settings.info: Optional. How the garment was measured, for example laid flat. It is what stops a shopper reading a flat measurement as a body measurement.
